title: LA SB346: Prohibits the use of deepfake material against students enrolled in K-12. (8/1/26)

key_definitions: deepfake: any audio or visual media in an electronic format, including any motion picture film or video recording, that is created, altered, or digitally manipulated in a manner that would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of the individual or that replaces an individual's likeness with another individual as depicted in the recording; deepfake does not include any material that constitutes a work of political, public interest, or newsworthy value, including commentary, criticism, satire, or parody, or that includes content, context, or a clear disclosure visible throughout the duration of the recording that would cause a reasonable person to understand that the audio or visual media is not a record of a real event (Sec. compliance_steps: Identify all students, faculty, administrative staff, and other employees who may create or use audio or visual media in the school context (Sec. A).
Establish policies prohibiting the use of deepfake material against K-12 students with intent to coerce, harass, intimidate, or maliciously disseminate or sell (Sec. A).
Train faculty, staff, and students on the definition of deepfake and the exclusions for political, public interest, newsworthy, commentary, criticism, satire, parody, or clear disclosure (Sec. B).
Implement review or monitoring of media used or shared in school contexts to detect deepfakes used against students (Sec. A).
Ensure any AI-generated media that could be considered deepfake includes clear disclosure visible throughout the duration or falls within exempt categories (Sec. B).
Monitor and comply with rules and regulations adopted by the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education in collaboration with the state Department of Education (Sec. C).

Passed 2026-05-29. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This law prohibits students, faculty members, administrative staff, and other employees at elementary or secondary schools from using deepfake material against a student enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve with the intent to coerce, harass, intimidate, or maliciously disseminate or sell the material. It defines deepfake and excludes certain political, public interest, newsworthy, commentary, criticism, satire, parody, or clearly disclosed material. It directs the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education and the state Department of Education to adopt implementing rules.

Who it applies to

  • Students at elementary or secondary schools
  • Faculty members at elementary or secondary schools
  • Members of administrative staff at elementary or secondary schools
  • Other employees at elementary or secondary schools

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • deepfake: any audio or visual media in an electronic format, including any motion picture film or video recording, that is created, altered, or digitally manipulated in a manner that would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of the individual or that replaces an individual's likeness with another individual as depicted in the recording; deepfake does not include any material that constitutes a work of political, public interest, or newsworthy value, including commentary, criticism, satire, or parody, or that includes content, context, or a clear disclosure visible throughout the duration of the recording that would cause a reasonable person to understand that the audio or visual media is not a record of a real event (Sec. B)

Obligations

  • The State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education, in collaboration with the state Department of Education, shall develop and adopt rules and regulations to implement the provisions of this Section (Sec. C)

Prohibitions

  • No student, faculty member, member of the administrative staff, or other employee at an elementary or secondary school shall use material considered to be a deepfake against a student enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve, with the intent to coerce, harass, intimidate, or maliciously disseminate or sell the material (Sec. A)

Penalties and enforcement

The statute does not specify penalties, an enforcement agency, or a private right of action. It directs the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education, in collaboration with the state Department of Education, to develop and adopt rules and regulations to implement the Section (Sec. C).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An elementary or secondary school must ensure that its students, faculty, administrative staff, and other employees do not use AI-generated deepfake material against any K-12 student with intent to coerce, harass, intimidate, or maliciously disseminate or sell (Sec. A).
  • AI-generated audio or visual media that falsely appears authentic or replaces a person's likeness is a deepfake unless it falls within the excluded categories of political, public interest, or newsworthy value, including commentary, criticism, satire, or parody, or includes a clear disclosure visible throughout the duration that would cause a reasonable person to understand it is not a real event (Sec. B).
  • Organisations deploying AI in schools should ensure any AI-generated media that could be considered deepfake includes clear disclosure visible throughout the duration or qualifies for an exclusion, to avoid falling within the prohibition (Sec. B).
  • The State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education will adopt rules that may impose additional requirements on schools regarding deepfake material (Sec. C).

Notable exemptions

  • Material that constitutes a work of political, public interest, or newsworthy value, including commentary, criticism, satire, or parody, or that includes content, context, or a clear disclosure visible throughout the duration of the recording that would cause a reasonable person to understand that the audio or visual media is not a record of a real event, is not a deepfake (Sec. B)

Compliance steps

  • Identify all students, faculty, administrative staff, and other employees who may create or use audio or visual media in the school context (Sec. A).
  • Establish policies prohibiting the use of deepfake material against K-12 students with intent to coerce, harass, intimidate, or maliciously disseminate or sell (Sec. A).
  • Train faculty, staff, and students on the definition of deepfake and the exclusions for political, public interest, newsworthy, commentary, criticism, satire, parody, or clear disclosure (Sec. B).
  • Implement review or monitoring of media used or shared in school contexts to detect deepfakes used against students (Sec. A).
  • Ensure any AI-generated media that could be considered deepfake includes clear disclosure visible throughout the duration or falls within exempt categories (Sec. B).
  • Monitor and comply with rules and regulations adopted by the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education in collaboration with the state Department of Education (Sec. C).
